candidates.title: Airbnb expands its internal AI platform to GPT-6 Astra and other frontier models
candidates.summary: Airbnb says engineers already use an internal AI tooling platform and remote agents powered by multiple OpenAI models, with broader frontier access now added.
candidates.what_changed: Airbnb says its engineers use an internal AI tooling platform to write software and create remote agents across several OpenAI model tiers, and has expanded access to GPT‑6 Astra.
candidates.why_it_matters: Large organizations increasingly treat models as **replaceable backends behind an internal agent platform**, rather than asking every developer to choose vendors and integrations independently.

candidates.title: Antigravity SDK can now run agent workflows locally and offline
candidates.summary: Google adds local-model execution through LiteRT, plus hybrid patterns where cloud models plan while local models handle privacy-sensitive or token-heavy work.
candidates.what_changed: The Antigravity SDK now supports local agentic workflows using models such as Gemma 4 through LiteRT, including fully offline execution and OpenAI-compatible local servers.
candidates.why_it_matters: Hybrid orchestration gives teams a new lever for **privacy, cost, and resilience** without forcing every task into the same inference environment.

candidates.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and Luna with a sharper cost ladder
candidates.summary: The two GPT-6 models bring Astra-era capabilities into faster and cheaper tiers, with materially lower API prices and cached-input costs.
candidates.what_changed: OpenAI released GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna in the API, Codex, and ChatGPT, positioning them as different capability/cost points below Astra.
candidates.why_it_matters: Model choice is becoming an architectural routing decision. The cost spread is large enough that teams should evaluate **which tasks genuinely need Sol-class reasoning and which can move to Luna**.

candidates.title: Greedy decoding is not deterministic across numeric precision
candidates.summary: A study finds identical prompts and models can diverge between BF16 and FP16, challenging assumptions that greedy decoding guarantees reproducible outputs.
candidates.what_changed: This paper shows that the same model, prompt, and greedy decoding algorithm can produce different outputs under BF16 versus FP16 on identical hardware.
candidates.why_it_matters: “Temperature zero” is not a reproducibility guarantee. Evals and production debugging should record **precision, kernels, batch conditions, and serving configuration** alongside model and prompt versions.
